purpose: This medication is a birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy. It may also be prescribed to help regulate your menstrual cycle, reduce painful periods, or treat acne in some cases. When taken correctly, it is a very effective way to avoid pregnancy.
how_it_works: This pill contains two hormones — estrogen and progestin — that work together to prevent pregnancy in a few ways. First, they stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. They also thicken the mucus in your cervix so sperm have a harder time getting through, and they thin the lining of your uterus to make it less likely for a fertilized egg to attach.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include nausea, breast tenderness or swelling, headaches, spotting or light bleeding between periods (especially in the first few months), mood changes, and decreased sex drive. Many of these tend to improve after the first couple of months as your body adjusts.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you smoke and are over 35 years old, as this significantly raises your risk of serious blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or certain cancers. This pill does NOT protect you from sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you have severe chest pain, sudden vision changes, severe headache, or leg pain or swelling.
typical_dosing: You take one pill by mouth every day at the same time each day. Most packs have 28 pills — 21 active hormone pills and 7 reminder (inactive) pills. You start a new pack right after finishing the old one without any break. Try to take it at the same time every day to make it as effective as possible.
